speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Finance in respect of the tender awarded by the Ministry of Home Affairs to ST Marine for the construction of 12 aluminium-hulled patrol boats (a) why his Ministry's Standing Committee on Debarment (SCOD) did not extend the disbarment of companies from tendering for Government contracts to cases where the companies or their senior executives had been convicted of corruption in private sector contracts; and (b) whether the notice of award was published no later than 72 days after the tender was awarded to ST Marine as required under the Government Procurement Regulations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Enforcement is by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) and adjudication of liability and the imposition of penalties for breach of the laws are carried out by the Courts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Companies or individuals convicted of corruption are thus penalised through the legal system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The penalties apply to cases involving both public and private sector-related contracts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The underlying rationale is because society, as a whole, is harmed by such conduct.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Debarment from participation in Government contracts is a separate and distinct exercise from Court proceedings and serves a different purpose.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Debarment is an administrative procedure by the Government to protect the Government’s interests as a service buyer, against those who have caused direct harm or losses to the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: It does not duplicate the Courts’ function of adjudication or punishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The grounds on which service providers can be debarred are made known publicly on the Government Electronic Business (GeBIZ) website and cover a variety of situations where Government interests have been harmed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: These include, for example, failure of a supplier to meet critical contractual obligations to a Government agency, abandonment or termination of a Government contract due to contractor default, among others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: As can be seen from the above, there must be a nexus to Government-related contracts before debarment can be applied.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The underlying rationale is to protect against suppliers who have caused direct harm or loss to the Government as a service buyer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In this case, the charges and convictions were against the individuals involved, namely, ST Marine's former group financial controller and six other former senior executives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: They were convicted in 2017 for offences committed in the period between 2000 and 2011, the most recent act thus being eight years ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The individuals involved ceased to be employed by ST Marine since between 2004 and 2014.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The company itself, ST Marine, which is a separate legal entity, did not have any charges or convictions against it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: A new Board of Directors of ST Marine was appointed as of 15 August 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Police Coast Guard tender was awarded in November 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In the Ministry of Home Affairs' (MHA’s) reply to The Straits Times on 9 March 2019, MHA had clarified that the contract was awarded to ST Marine on 26 November 2018 and the notice of award was published on the GeBIZ website the next day on 27 November 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The date of award of the tender was initially incorrectly shown as 27 July 2018 on the GeBIZ website and this has been rectified.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just have a few supplementary questions to follow up.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What would be the considerations to set past corruption offences involving private sector contracts at "Nil", to provide no consideration for that, and only to consider corruption related to previous Government contracts?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let us make a distinction between past convictions in relation to private sector contracts and past convictions in relation to public sector contracts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, past convictions in relation to public sector contracts – that is clear.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Now, this does not mean to say that the committees or people looking at the SCOD, looking at the contracts or whoever is awarding the tender, cannot consider past convictions of private sector contracts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that is not an exercise in debarment, under the debarment policy parameters.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That would be an exercise in looking to see holistically whether there is a risk to contract performance, to contract integrity, and reputational risk.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that is an exercise in relation to assessment of risk for contract performance and contract integrity, rather than an exercise of debarment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I understand the Minister has said that specifically with regard to the procedure for debarment, Government contracts – public sector contracts – are taken into consideration, not private sector contracts and there are other mechanisms or processes in procurement where private sector corruption in the past can be taken into account.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I would just like to sort of go deeper on this point: why can the debarment process run by SCOD not take into account past private sector corruption offences?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Why is it only taking into account past public sector corruption offences?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Will that be something that the Government is prepared to review, going forward?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I should just thank the Minister for her response.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just to clarify on that, my purpose is for the purpose of debarment because past public sector corruption cases are potential grounds for debarment because of various risks that the Government may be exposed to if the tender is awarded to that company.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, why would not past private sector corruption cases also similarly give rise to grounds for potential debarment under the SCOD debarment procedures?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: My question was: in the Member's context, what is the purpose of the debarment?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when the Member suggests that there should be debarment in relation to private sector contracts, what is the underlying purpose of the debarment?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if it is to protect the Government, then there is not a nexus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I am just trying to understand the purpose for which the Member is suggesting we should have debarment, so that I can address the question.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The purpose for which I am suggesting the debarment can be considered is essentially protection of the Government's interest because if debarment can be considered for companies involved in past public sector offences.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Well, if the company has been involved in past private sector corruption offences, then, presumably, that creates a possibility that they may also expose the Government to some risk if they take on a public sector contract.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, my purpose is basically protection of the Government, and to have a debarment process that considers both Government and private sector past corruption offences because past private sector corruption offences may be grounds to suppose that there is some risk even if that company were to undertake a Government contract.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if the purpose is adjudication and punishment, that is dealt with by the Courts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Insofar as the purpose is to protect the Government's interest by preventing the supplier from getting fresh contracts, that is where debarment applies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As I had explained earlier, that is an exercise in assessment of risk of performance, or risk of integrity to the contract, or reputational risk.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, either way, the purpose is addressed, whether it be Court, debarment or overall holistic assessment.
